head: 6c38b2507abf355bfe351d51a375165ec0c54ca3
title: Adopt authentic artwork and shared creative-world contracts
pr_body:

Adopt the owner's Connected Creative Universe directive for Workstreams A–F. The standard establishes permanent protection of original artwork and the 2D direction for new games. It assigns ownership of drawing, identity, worlds, animation, game bindings, recovery and migration review.

## Implementation and integration

Foundation for the drawing and integrated picker PRs. Base protected main `bc602f1ede502f398308ad56f973c4bf7997ff08`. The Learning Workspace series #192–195 owns temporary working paper and keeps its independent release sequence.

## Evidence and documentation

The documentation range check verifies routing and links for head `6c38b2507abf355bfe351d51a375165ec0c54ca3`. The product doctrine, new standard, ADR, index, registry, PR template and maintenance process now describe version pinning and source ownership.

## Preview, acceptance and delivery

Documentation only. Rendered and storage acceptance belongs to the dependent source PRs. This PR requests review and authorizes no deployment, spending, production bridge or family activation.

head: 81767273becb93bd9bae9a46725b26af644e4578
title: Set the creative asset and world standard and preserve exact reviewed originals
pr_body:
## Intent and resulting behavior

Establish the owner-approved Creative Asset & World Design Standard for A–F. The reviewed adult workshop import retains the same PNG bytes that the operator authorized. Its format check rejects files with embedded file-detail chunks or trailing bytes before sending a digest.

## Implementation and integration

Base `bc602f1ede502f398308ad56f973c4bf7997ff08`. Head `81767273becb93bd9bae9a46725b26af644e4578`. This head includes both parallel standards proposals through Git ancestry, #196 at `6c38b2507abf355bfe351d51a375165ec0c54ca3` and #197 at `637914ba850d42cb64ee7a45e071b88573c80716`. Both documentation entry points resolve to one canonical standard. This is the foundation for the integrated creative editor PR. The import uses the existing private art store, digest approval, trusted device unlock and selected profile. Historical beta rasters retain their original stored representation. The parallel learning stack #192–195 owns transient scratchpad work.

## Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Local check on this tree | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact accepted bytes, digest-only host request, refusal and concurrent profile switch | `CHROMIUM_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium node tests/beta-reviewed-art-browser.cjs` | Passed using real PNG/IndexedDB, synthetic origin and simulated authorization responses |
| Container acceptance and rejection | `node --import tsx tests/beta-reviewed-png.test.ts` | Both tests passed |

Try a file with embedded metadata. Private DEV access, owner acceptance, deployed TEST and physical device verification are pending.

head: 5a0970e487d8630eeafd8f8792b092c17936c425
title: Creative Universe A: keep editable original drawings and revision history
pr_body:
## Intent and resulting behavior

Workstream A of the Connected Creative Universe directive lets a child continue a kept drawing from its original brush strokes. My Art offers an eraser, clear paper and a **Keep drawing** action on supported sketches. Saving a change produces an immutable child-owned image revision. Each previously saved scene or adventure keeps its selected version.

## Implementation and integration

This draft depends on the Creative Asset & World Design Standard at `6c38b2507abf355bfe351d51a375165ec0c54ca3`. The candidate is `5a0970e487d8630eeafd8f8792b092c17936c425`. Its application source matches the first implementation head, `dc1dba8a6c4d139ca887aaf3f8bc1eb622d7ecfb`. The private drawing store owns the exact kept PNG, including its bounded, versioned ancillary crayon chunk. The existing source ID, source digest, image capacity checks and family transfer transactions apply. Opening first validates record bounds and checksum, then compares every pixel of the rendered strokes with the decoded original. A differing renderer or invalid source leaves the exact saved image available in picture tools. Uploads and older images retain their existing raster representation. This is additive and requires no database migration. An earlier client can display and back up the same PNG. Follow-on work can use the drawing dialog and the shared PNG checksum helper.

## Evidence

The fixture makes a synthetic pebble with boots through real pointer input. It saves and reloads the sketch, checks erasing and undo/redo, compares original bytes after a new revision, restores the exported library into an empty browser context, and checks mismatched replay rejection and zero POSTs. The phone screenshot exercises the recovered source. The desktop screenshot exercises the drawing activity. [Desktop drawing](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/blob/dc1dba8a6c4d139ca887aaf3f8bc1eb622d7ecfb/docs/creative-universe/evidence/editable-sketch.png) · [Restored phone drawing](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/blob/dc1dba8a6c4d139ca887aaf3f8bc1eb622d7ecfb/docs/creative-universe/evidence/restored-sketch-phone.png)

All of the following local checks passed against clean corrected source `5a0970e487d8630eeafd8f8792b092c17936c425`.

| Check | Result and scope |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run build` | TypeScript and production Vite build passed. The served build receipt reports the exact commit and a clean tree. |
| `npm run test:art` | All 24 drawing, binding and scene-art unit checks passed. |
| `npm run test:art-browser` | All seven browser scripts passed. Coverage includes 46 private-storage contracts, draft recovery, revision lineage, real local PNG codecs, explicit scene bindings, profile changes, desktop and emulated touch flows and the new crayon round trip. |
| `npm run docs:check -- --base 6c38b2507abf355bfe351d51a375165ec0c54ca3 --head 5a0970e487d8630eeafd8f8792b092c17936c425` | Zero errors and zero review reminders. |

The linked development captures show the same drawing and controls exercised by the exact-head run. The latter captured fresh desktop and phone images with SHA-256 digests `176e9850c8a04de5ad2abde359b31d7e13eabd68c61ec26c2d87d94fd9d8950f` and `e446693fda63ccdc50e1d6216995865027e956b437fff6f050a5a5b456351772` respectively.

### CI coverage correction

The first Arcade run stopped in prepare's `npm run test:ci`. The added browser journey raised the creative leaf-command count to 66 while the coverage fixture still expected 65. Local reproduction at the first head failed exactly one of 118 tests. The downstream aggregates rejected the absent plan and shard receipts as designed. The corrected head updates the expected count to 66 and the validation review record. All 118 CI contract tests passed locally on the corrected head. The production build, 24 art unit tests, all seven art browser scripts, and range docs check passed again at that clean head. The exact-head screenshot digests also reproduced. The new hosted Arcade run is pending. [Corrected-head run](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/actions/runs/45748427756) [Initial failed prepare](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/actions/runs/45746979497/job/139665294953)

## Preview and acceptance

Local production-bundle Chromium testing uses generated fixture marks and an emulated phone viewport. For manual acceptance, open My Art → Draw here, draw and keep a picture, reopen **Keep drawing**, undo a stroke and save a second version. Both images should remain selectable. Export and restore the library on another local test profile to check editable recovery. Hosted DEV, TEST/UAT, physical tablet, owner acceptance and production release evidence are pending.

## Documentation review

Reviewed the product doctrine, current architecture, Art Studio gold standard, child-interface requirements, storage and recovery contract, permanent Creative Asset & World Design Standard and the CI/release contracts. Updated the Art Studio feature contract and routed the new browser journey to its review area. The package adds the regression to the existing artwork CI gate. The established release process, product intent and validation policy still apply.

## Delivery and follow-up

Source implementation is proposed in this draft. The existing private storage and reader remain the recovery path across rollback. No worker pin, service configuration, deployment, spend or family activation is included. General generated-game artwork delivery still requires independent qualification.

head: 114e03b44253f85a715fe6f0d84e868c8b573f55
title: Draw and reuse movement paths for private artwork in Creative Studio
pr_body:
## Intent and resulting behavior

A child can select an original picture or cutout in Creative Studio and draw a movement path for it with a mouse, touch or direction buttons. The child chooses its name and speed. Adding the path writes editable Move blocks to the selected actor’s script. The saved picture remains pinned to its original reference. A kept scene makes its path available for reuse in another private-art scene.

## Implementation and integration

Workstream C depends on `feat/creative-drawing-source` at `5a0970e487d8630eeafd8f8792b092c17936c425`. The final runtime source is `73779309bfa22cc45e65ecda9968e81e12a77643`. The evidence and CI contract head is `114e03b44253f85a715fe6f0d84e868c8b573f55`. This PR owns the motion composer, optional Repeat-group name and owner-scoped kept-revision reads from both scene storage authorities. Coordinate overlapping `creation/ui.ts`, `model.ts` and the review fingerprints with B, D and F before integration.

The path uses up to 24 relative moves with explicit durations. Scene playback uses the existing fixed-clock engine. Copies receive new block IDs, so changing the kept source leaves the destination intact. A temporary path pad stays in memory until added or closed. Undo, draft recovery, scene bundles, private references and explicit Keep flow through current contracts.

## Evidence

| Claim | Exact-source evidence | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build and deterministic movement | `npm run build`, `npm run test:creation` on `fe015626` | Typecheck and Vite passed. All 90 tests passed with the local fixture server available. The first network-restricted run could not run the generated-manifest fixture suite. |
| Render, reuse and undo | `node tests/creation-motion-browser.cjs` on the built application | Chromium traced a path with the mouse, used the keyboard arrows, stepped playback in reduced-motion mode and finished at the expected stage position. The second scene copied the kept path with fresh IDs. No POST requests occurred. |
| Portrait regression | The first expanded sweep at `fe015626` found the 768 × 1024 bundled starter too small when Step was available for every actor. | `73779309` confines that shortcut to private artwork. All eight responsive first-learner journeys, native Chromium 150% zoom and the focused motion journey passed on the corrected build. All three screenshots were byte-identical on the corrected build. A Chromium touch-event drag on a tablet viewport also passed on the first build. |
| Visual evidence | [Desktop pad](docs/creative-universe/evidence/motion/draw-a-path.png), [390 px pad](docs/creative-universe/evidence/motion/draw-a-path-phone.png), [playback](docs/creative-universe/evidence/motion/path-playback.png) | Synthetic artwork, desktop Chromium and phone viewport emulation. |
| Creative shard coverage | The first coverage expectation retained the previous 65 leaf commands. The drawing and motion browser journeys add one creative leaf each. | The corrected expectation is 67 creative, 43 browser, 12 learning and 2 notifications. All 118 CI contract tests passed locally. The checker retains its missing and duplicate command negatives. |
| Review and regression routing | `node scripts/ci/suites.mjs` and exact-range `npm run docs:check` | Existing Creative Studio unit and browser suites include the new regressions. Documentation reports zero errors. |

## Preview and acceptance

Private DEV, TEST and owner review remain pending. To review, open a drawing in Creative Studio, choose **Draw a path**, trace or use arrows, add it and Keep the scene. Open another drawing, select **Paths from my kept scenes** and play the copied path. The current implementation moves a whole actor. Physical rigs retain their existing editor and runtime. No real family data or physical-device acceptance was part of the local checks.

## Documentation review

Consulted the artwork, scene, storage, release, child interface and Creative Asset & World standards. Updated the [scene contract](docs/creation-studio/README.md), [drawn-path guide](docs/creation-studio/DRAWN_PATHS.md), architecture and review records. Package changes add coverage within existing CI shard assignments and deployment governance.

## Delivery and follow-up

Draft source for review. Hosted qualification, production deployment and external family activation are pending. The changes add no model calls, billed operations or generated-game artwork delivery.

head: 80fab162842b2cc99bb9e0dfdae5e7ed17ab2b10
title: Qualify a pinned private sprite slot with the offline 2D sandbox
pr_body:
## Intent and resulting behavior

Owner-authorized Workstream E calls for scoped delivery of private artwork in generated 2D games, pending independent qualification. This PR exercises a single selected synthetic sprite with the archived v2 runtime. An actual keyboard input moves the public fixture actor. A trusted compositor paints the exact selected pixels at that actor's reported position.

## Implementation and integration

Stacked on [the creative universe contract, #196](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/pull/196), base `6c38b2507abf355bfe351d51a375165ec0c54ca3`. Source head `80fab162842b2cc99bb9e0dfdae5e7ed17ab2b10`. The QA harness receives validated display commands through the existing QA capture. Private bytes, database handles, owner and family IDs stay outside the generated iframe and worker. The reviewed slot binds a public alias to an artifact digest and game revision. The host binding adds the exact selected asset revision and content hash. A fresh permitted play session is required. No schema migration, hosted handler, production switch, paid operation or release workflow is introduced.

## Evidence

| Criterion | Local check at the source head above | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Approved 2D behavior and compatibility | `CHROMIUM_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium npm run test:generated-art` | Existing desktop, tablet, phone, unknown-image/decode and retained-runtime checks plus the new offline fixture pass. |
| Selected pixels in motion | Ordinary right-arrow input in the archived sandbox, revalidated image command, aspect-fit and center/transparent-margin pixel assertions | Pass. The workshop is approved Jems environment artwork. The small drawing is synthetic. [Rendered compositor capture](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/blob/80fab162842b2cc99bb9e0dfdae5e7ed17ab2b10/docs/game-intelligence/evidence/generated-slot-compositor.png). |
| Isolation, exact pins and lifecycle | Wrong family, owner, game revision, artifact, slot, selected revision and digest, denied consent, unrecognized alias and revoked session | Pass. The iframe receives no selected raster or local owner ID. Zero network requests after the fixture shell opens. |
| Static checks | `npm run typecheck` and `npm run docs:check` | Pass. Documentation checker reports zero errors and reminders. |

One early harness iteration failed because tsx's function-name helper was missing from a Playwright-serialized fixture callback. The synthetic page provides that helper. This adds coverage to the existing generated-art suite. The initial 0ce941d hosted run failed its exact browser-group count assertion (the new generated-art leaf raises it from 43 to 44). Its PR-range docs check also required the new contract in the routed documentation index. Head 80fab16 updates the explicit count and reference index. The locally reproduced CI orchestration suite passes 118 checks, and the base-to-head documentation check passes with zero errors or reminders. CI selection and shard configuration remain unchanged.

## Preview and acceptance

The production application has no entrance to this qualification tool. The screenshot and repeatable browser command above cover the proposed design on local Chromium. Hosted DEV/TEST, independent security review, physical devices, production deployment and family activation are outside this evidence.

## Documentation and context review

The [scoped delivery contract](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/blob/80fab162842b2cc99bb9e0dfdae5e7ed17ab2b10/docs/game-intelligence/PRIVATE-SPRITE-QUALIFICATION.md) records authorship, version pins, limitations and deployment boundaries. The reference registry routes the new contract and tooling. The generation, validation, delivery and routing reviews cover this diff.

## Delivery and follow-up

This draft is available for source and independent security review. General delivery needs a scoped production frame transport, camera/layer composition, persisted grant and consent lifecycle, recovery, independent hosted qualification and release approval. The separate picture-hunt feature uses trusted local scene storage and can be reviewed independently.

head: ba220630d229ad5cf46ceca3dcb8fc3afc3a2223
title: Validate reviewed PNG scanlines before preserving exact originals
pr_body:
## Intent and resulting behavior

The restricted family uploader can keep the exact PNG approved for that family. This change qualifies the image portion of the file before requesting its digest approval. The color model determines which palette and transparency records apply. A streaming check verifies the expected number of scanline bytes, including interlaced passes. Ordinary decoding, private storage, the active explorer check and the adult unlock continue through the existing uploader.

## Implementation and integration

Direct dependency on #198 at `81767273becb93bd9bae9a46725b26af644e4578`. Scoped head `ba220630d229ad5cf46ceca3dcb8fc3afc3a2223`. The original-byte uploader, digest review API and Chromium acceptance test belong to #198. This follow-up extends its file validation and existing positive and negative fixtures. It introduces no storage migration, external dependencies or generated-game access.

## Evidence

| Check on the scoped source | Local outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `node --import tsx tests/beta-reviewed-png.test.ts` | Three tests pass, covering exact truecolor, indexed transparency and interlaced rasters, file details, truncated containers, palette applicability and expected scanline counts |
| `CHROMIUM_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium node tests/beta-reviewed-art-browser.cjs` | Real file input and IndexedDB pass exact bytes, digest-only authorization, refusal and explorer change using synthetic fixtures |
| `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build:family-beta` | Pass. Vite reports its existing chunk-size advisory |
| `npm run docs:check` | Pass after reviewing the experience and validation entries |

## Preview and acceptance

The operator input uses its existing presentation. No new visual surface or screenshot. In private DEV, try an approved synthetic indexed or truecolor PNG through the guardian input and compare its stored digest with the reviewed digest. A PNG with incomplete picture data should stop before any approval request. The new check requires browser support for streaming DEFLATE. Private DEV, owner acceptance and hosted TEST remain pending.

## Documentation review

The architecture corrects its historical raster-reencoding statement. The operator guide identifies the indexed-color palette and documents preparing a separate image-only export for review. Rejected input leaves the source file in the guardian's possession. Previously saved raster-only uploads retain their historical stored representation.

## Delivery and follow-up

Draft source and offline validation. The existing digest authorization, family privacy settings, device qualification and release process govern any rollout. No deployment, family data transfer, traffic cutover or paid operation was performed.

head: 16c4132d92e8c9d21ae20b604238656184e42fa7

pr_body:
## Intent and resulting behavior

A child can reopen a layered crayon drawing, keep another revision and use a drawn path in a Creative Studio actor program. The host can select from a versioned collection of four Jems worlds. This prerequisite supplies the catalogue, artwork and provenance for the downstream stage renderer. Reviewed family PNGs keep their exact approved bytes after bounded validation.

## Implementation and integration

The integration base is #198 at `81767273becb93bd9bae9a46725b26af644e4578`. The source head is `16c4132d92e8c9d21ae20b604238656184e42fa7` and its tree is `2645d38f05b0e02daea213bbd49656056d2a1175`.

| Input | Scope and ownership |
| --- | --- |
| #199, incorporated through #201 | My Art owns editable crayon sources and immutable private PNG revisions. |
| #201, `e1b67c17fa3c2ff103b221173cf476ac82d09206` | Creative Studio owns named paths represented by ordinary editable movement blocks, their actor programs and stored revisions. |
| #200, `19189bf436369bd6deca26b9fa6fd635b04c1317` | The world catalogue owns 48 original files, including 32 props. The stage owner qualifies their composition with real actors. |
| #204, `ba220630d229ad5cf46ceca3dcb8fc3afc3a2223` | Reviewed-family import owns PNG envelope and raster admission ahead of local storage. |
 
Workstreams A, B and C supply these interfaces to D, E and F. The downstream activity integration and the separate learning-workspace stack have their own PRs. #205 is outside this input cutoff.

## Evidence

All local checks below used the exact source head listed above. The two illustrated and drawing paths use synthetic artwork.

| Check | Result and limits |

| TypeScript and frontend production build | Passed. Generated build-info identifies the exact head and a clean checkout. The first sandboxed attempt stopped when the offline-build Git metadata subprocess was denied. The normal build completed on rerun with the required sandbox permission. |

| Crayon and path Chromium journeys | Both passed. My Art covered editing, fractional transparency, undo/redo after reload, version lineage, byte-exact backup recovery, foreign-raster rejection and zero POSTs. Scene playback covered accessible controls, authored path reuse, immutable pins, deterministic position and undo. |

pr_body:

After a child keeps or imports a picture in My Art, **Make it move** opens on that picture. Jump, Bounce, Spin, Dance, Left, Right, Float, Shake and Path use the child's marks. Save keeps an exact movement version. From a scene actor, **Try the saved parts** revalidates the original and rig hash, then opens a read-only physics preview. **Back to scene** returns to its existing code. Scene blocks continue to move its composite sprite. **Use in Creative Studio** plays that version in its chosen world. **Bring its parts to life** opens the manual parts editor for independently moving cutouts, hinges, wheels and motors.

## Implementation and integration

Source `b9843081251ef61abfa52541e8e868688dae5007` on #207 at `16c4132d92e8c9d21ae20b604238656184e42fa7`. #207 reconciles #199 editable PNGs, #201 named coded paths, #200 illustrated assets and #204 family admission on #198. Explicit scene roles round-trip independently of mechanics. #209, #211 and #213–216 offer parallel UI, artwork, library and game changes and need a single integration decision before promotion. #202 and #206 are independent generated-game qualification work.

head: ca76b5b151d4de61a5da0d66f64093530fdc1f78
title: Reuse a child’s pinned artwork across My Art, movement, worlds and local 2D games
pr_body:
## Intent and resulting behavior

A child can keep a drawing, name it, choose its exact revision in another activity, and see where it was used. The drawing, its edits and its saved movements remain in the existing private drawing and scene authorities. One rock can decorate a world, follow an authored path and serve as a local game's collectible. Editing that rock leaves the earlier adventures pinned. A freshly restored profile recovers the original bytes and editable strokes.

## Implementation and integration

Head `ca76b5b151d4de61a5da0d66f64093530fdc1f78` on [combined dependency PR #209](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/pull/209) at `e370770e3ad757bc13308c0f19b36e8c98832d80`. Protected main at the integration cutoff is `bc602f1ede502f398308ad56f973c4bf7997ff08`. Incorporated inputs include the three converged standards #196–198, editable drawings #199, original illustrated worlds #200, movement #201, offline generated-slot experiment #202 and reviewed PNG admission #204. The generic pointer helper matches learning #203; the learning scratchpad has its own lifetime.

My Art owns images, revisions, classification and discovery. Creative Studio owns instances, programs, pinned backgrounds and world layout. The game host owns explicit compatible mechanics. Storage owns reference validation, archive and recovery. The compatibility reader accepts both candidate semantic and role spellings and rejects conflicting aliases. Contextual role alone cannot change the engine. An original download remains distinct from exporting the visible pixels of a sketch.

Parallel #205–208 and #210–214 contain overlapping alternatives. The release maintainer must reconcile any selected alternative before merging to main. Their additional experimental formats or generated-game adapters cannot be assumed interchangeable. Prior released readers and private-family handling require separate rollout review. Retired original bytes from older family uploads cannot be reconstructed.

## Evidence

[Acceptance, reproducible commands and screenshots](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/blob/ca76b5b151d4de61a5da0d66f64093530fdc1f78/docs/creative-universe/EVIDENCE.md) · [Destination matrix](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/blob/ca76b5b151d4de61a5da0d66f64093530fdc1f78/docs/creative-universe/STANDARD.md#destination-compatibility) · [Offline review](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/blob/ca76b5b151d4de61a5da0d66f64093530fdc1f78/docs/ui-review/README.md#connected-creative-universe)

| Behavior | Local evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Artwork, ownership and recovery | Four synthetic editable subjects are selected in game, scene, animation and world contexts. Browser checks verify exact initial and updated pins, original SHA and stroke recovery, archive visibility, stale owner denial and fresh-device restore. |
| Picker and activity return | Desktop and phone screenshots, actual thumbnails, version family and category filtering. Drawing inside the picker returns selection to the same activity. The game idea and existing game remain recoverable after a separate picture hunt. |
| Illustrated stages and placements | Four painted stages, 32 transparent props, keyboard position controls, private backdrop, layer visibility, older classic worlds, export, restore and pending thumbnail disposal. |
| Local 2D play and movement | The selected original is the actual picture-hunt target. Play and Keep an explicit replacement. Rally requires a valid car rig. Movement programs preserve identity and author-selected behavior. |
| Independent generation contract | Offline v2 host compositor exercises a bounded selected slot in isolation. The application does not enable general production delivery of private drawings to generated code. |
| Orchestration and documentation | Required coverage counts 71 creative, 44 browser, 12 learning and 2 notification leaf commands. All original commands remain. The exact upstream-to-head documentation range passes. |

### Source heads and dependent PRs

| Workstream | Input PR heads | Shared application head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | #199 `5a0970e487d8630eeafd8f8792b092c17936c425`, #204 `ba220630d229ad5cf46ceca3dcb8fc3afc3a2223` | #215 `ca76b5b151d4de61a5da0d66f64093530fdc1f78` |
| B and F | #200 `19189bf436369bd6deca26b9fa6fd635b04c1317` | #215 connects actual layered stages, custom placements and shared picker |
| C | #201 `114e03b44253f85a715fe6f0d84e868c8b573f55` | #215 adds movement discovery and recovers pinned path use |
| D | #209 `e370770e3ad757bc13308c0f19b36e8c98832d80` | #215 `ca76b5b151d4de61a5da0d66f64093530fdc1f78` |
| E | #202 `80fab162842b2cc99bb9e0dfdae5e7ed17ab2b10` | #215 supplies the local game entrances and explicit Keep |
| Shared doctrine and upload foundation | #196 `6c38b2507abf355bfe351d51a375165ec0c54ca3`, #197 `637914ba850d42cb64ee7a45e071b88573c80716`, #198 `81767273becb93bd9bae9a46725b26af644e4578` | Reconciled through #209 |

### Exact-head local results

The production build and typecheck passed. The art unit suite passed 33/33, creation passed 90/90 and CI orchestration passed 118/118. All art and creation browser scripts passed, including 57 storage checks, four original/edited recoveries, eight creation recovery journeys, desktop and tablet gameplay, eight learner viewports and native Chromium 150% zoom. Complete backup and adult transfer passed separately. The upstream-to-head and protected-main-to-head documentation checks both reported zero errors.

The standalone HTML represents this PR head, has SHA-256 `223eba75fdd9192f62693ec1fa2242c4c298091cd84924f8cd38f63bb83136a0` and embeds 392 assets. Its smoke, integration and picker journeys passed with zero external requests. The local managed Chromium blocks file navigation by administrative policy. The tests loaded the exact HTML through the repository's in-memory launcher. The [GitHub artifact workflow](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/actions/runs/45749318444) tracks the independently built file-open qualification.

The GitHub merge candidate observed for the stack was `ac217b1910cfa241aa7b2a36e3484b26516fb889`. The 17 hosted checks for the PR head were queued at the last local evidence cut. No hosted pass or private DEV deployment receipt is claimed.

## Preview and acceptance

Open the offline UI sandbox in **Populated**, select **My Art · choose a saved creation**, then use My Rock in a local picture hunt. The package uses four synthetic editable drawings and the production UI. Hosted DEV/TEST and physical-device checks remain pending. The hosted checks tab and Actions artifacts report their own status for this SHA.

## Documentation review

Reviewed the standard, destination matrix, original and visible-only downloads, trusted game bindings, world art, storage, decision, architecture, delivery, evidence and context registry.

## Delivery and follow-up

Draft source review. No production deployment, paid operation, transfer of family data, or external activation occurred. Independent security and release qualification are required for any future general generated-game delivery.

head: 1ac8f5b55caaec57dbd9fe637a46e6b8c8aaea0a
title: Workstream E: pin original artwork to playable 2D game tests
pr_body:
## Intent and resulting behavior

A child can choose a My Art revision from a drawing, a new idea or an existing game's tools, assign it one of nine roles and say what it should do. One rock can be both a collectible and an obstacle. The plan stays with that game. Replacing a picture in a role requires an explicit choice and preserves older game tests.

## Implementation and integration

The source is `1ac8f5b55caaec57dbd9fe637a46e6b8c8aaea0a`. The application base is #213 at `c4214a037088d589557edb401b1fbf6ae29cf108`, which integrates the #206 renderer. Workstream D owns the private drawing catalog, logical identity and lineage. E owns notebook roles, exact version bindings and their resolution for a game. #202 and #212 contain parallel test hosts. #215 at `ca76b5b151d4de61a5da0d66f64093530fdc1f78` is a separate integration on #209 with its own game-art picker. Select and reconcile the shared catalog and notebook formats before a protected-main merge. Protected application main was `bc602f1ede502f398308ad56f973c4bf7997ff08`. The private worker main was `dddf53dbc76796be19782c1bb5bbb99b86e99909`.

The existing private drawing store owns original bytes. The notebook records the original and selected revision fingerprints and game-local roles. The standalone offline review build verifies the game program and exact synthetic originals, strips editor metadata, and supplies visible rasters to an opaque scripts-only frame. Its generated worker receives bounded handles and aspect ratios. A new launch checks the current scope and the exact stored bytes again. The normal application holds online Build and retry for plans with selected artwork before spending admission.

## Evidence

| Criterion | Local observation and limits |
| --- | --- |
| Actual playable rendering | Playwright compares the complete initial 720 × 400 canvas to a direct composite. The rocket is the player, the rock appears as both collectible and obstacle, the dragon is a character, and the valley is the background. Real input exercises scoring, collision and winning. |
| Improvements and recovery | A faster reviewed program keeps the same five pins. The earlier program remains playable after Keep and reload. Tests cover explicit replacement, notebook copies, original-byte restore, broken backups, archive and missing images. |
| Scope and privacy | Synthetic checks cover origin/profile mismatch, copied and forged handles, wrong revisions and hashes, denied unbound draw commands, stale authorization, profile teardown, opaque frame isolation and outbound request monitoring. The existing hostile-module browser tests exercise blocked network/DOM access and termination. |
| Regression | Generated-art, drawing browser and unit suites, 48 generation/readiness and storage-related contract tests, complete recovery, adult transfer, normal/family builds and documentation checks passed locally. The standard and family builds were checked for exclusion of the review fixture. All 32 Studio unit tests, the desktop and mobile Studio journeys, and the remote ACK/Keep/recovery fixture also passed. A legacy desktop v1 learning preview timed out on its first run. That case passed on unmodified reruns of this head and its base. The v2 desktop and mobile learning previews passed on the first run. |

[Four rendered captures and reproduction instructions](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/tree/1ac8f5b55caaec57dbd9fe637a46e6b8c8aaea0a/docs/game-art/evidence)

## Preview and acceptance

Run `npm run test:game-art` using the locked dependencies and Playwright Chromium. The test builds the standalone synthetic preview. The protocol guide includes directions for manual play and replay. The normal build includes the planning journey. Local samples use four synthetic originals and two archived-runtime programs and make no provider calls. The renderer supports eight active images including the background.

Private hosted DEV, owner visual and interactive acceptance, physical devices, TEST and authenticated worker/sandbox qualification are pending. The local test supplies no receipt for hosted generation. The previous public deployment observation was `aa56b60abe152e750f9f0b5e8949bdb44be53196`.

## Documentation review

Reviewed the product, architecture, delivery, My Art, Creative Studio, child interface, privacy, Game Intelligence and premium generation contracts. The canonical Creative Asset & World Design Standard now specifies D/E ownership. The linked protocol, decision and evidence record the local capability, threat model and release gates. Nine documentation areas were refreshed. The base-to-head documentation check passed with 127 registered documents.

## Delivery and follow-up

Draft for integration and independent review. Before enabling hosted binding, qualify authenticated cross-family grants, withdrawal during play, cache isolation, learning-host continuity, interruption and scoped delivery. Keep private pixels out of all downstream model-facing captures. Persistent thumbnails and generic rig adapters remain outside this reviewed implementation. Older strict notebook readers reject the new field after first write. Qualify a compatible rollback reader before household rollout. Deployment, worker updates, paid generation and external family activation require separate controls.

head: aea3cead13d164b7ce93fbded5fee6ecd9896eca
title: Creative Studio · Build, keep and reuse personalized 2D worlds
pr_body:
## What the child can do

Begin with Enchanted Gem Forest, Inventor’s Workshop, Cloud Kingdom, Moon Adventure or a white stage. Pick scenery across the four collections, add personal artwork, turn or resize a placement, change its visual layer, give that instance a code block, play and keep the result. **Use this world** starts an independent scene from its exact kept revision, including when a newer draft exists.

## Dependencies and ownership

Review on top of #211 at `1969df66038d5d1e9b77534f3d08d5d0c01b3380`. It brings #196 (standard), #200 (versioned worlds and 32 props) and #208 (owner-scoped private artwork and picker). This PR carries forward the regression in #205. F owns composition and kept-world reuse. B owns the art registry and D owns personal asset selection. Local and IndexedDB persistence use the existing scene authority. The shared drawing input helper carries coordinates. Learning scratchpads, rewards and challenge geometry retain their existing contracts.

## Evidence

Tested application head `7c31f717712a23001c0d95ed9ed88fa3e4ade3a3`. Review head `aea3cead13d164b7ce93fbded5fee6ecd9896eca` includes the final evidence and documentation registry. Local production build, 92 scene tests, 27 My Art tests, 17 Pal integration tests, three illustrated stage layouts, touch and keyboard placement, challenge and recovery browser journeys, and IndexedDB kept-version reconstruction passed. The standalone regression recovered the original bytes and compared the personal landscape with its stage and decoded video export. The local standalone uses its in-memory transport. CI builds the exact PR-head standalone download and opens it directly. The documentation range check passed.

[Rendered screenshots, exported video and test instructions](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/blob/aea3cead13d164b7ce93fbded5fee6ecd9896eca/docs/creation-studio/evidence/world-composition/README.md) · [Canonical standard](https://github.com/jzwyrzyk/family-game-factory/blob/aea3cead13d164b7ce93fbded5fee6ecd9896eca/docs/creative-universe/STANDARD.md#building-and-keeping-a-world)

## Release

Draft source for integration. The blank stage starts with one editable gem under the retained schema. Owner art sign-off, physical device and hosted DEV/TEST acceptance, and mixed-version rollback qualification remain open. Generated-game delivery currently has separate scoped sprite qualification. General world composition delivery, production promotion and external family activation require their own qualification and release decisions.

Parallel integrations #215 and #216 use separate library/game contracts. #216 exercises individual pinned backgrounds and object roles in an offline game test. Neither PR supplies a reviewed adapter for an entire kept Studio composition. Reconcile shared scene/catalogue representations when selecting a protected-main integration. The currently integrated generated-companion browser test passed replacement, cancellation, Undo, movement, Keep, owner checks, history and reload with zero POSTs.
